# Executive Summary

This report delivers an empirical, observational analysis of the German biomedical research ecosystem supported by the **Else Kröner-Fresenius-Stiftung (EKFS)** and the **Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG)**.

## Core Research Question
> *“How are EKFS- and DFG-funded biomedical researchers, projects, institutions, research topics, publications, and collaboration communities connected, and how do those relationships change across funding source and time?”*

## Key Findings & Structural Insights
1. **Funder Overlap & Complementarity**: EKFS grants strongly complement federal DFG programs by providing strategic clinician scientist fellowships, translational stepping stones, and key high-risk clinical infrastructure.
2. **Funding Trajectories & Sequencing**: Rather than operating in isolated silos, investigators exhibit systematic multi-stage trajectories where early EKFS clinician scientist support frequently precedes larger DFG individual awards (Sachbeihilfe/Emmy Noether), or established DFG investigators acquire targeted EKFS translational project grants.
3. **Network Modularity & Community Clusters**: Coauthorship clustering reveals coherent interdisciplinary clinical and basic science clusters centered around major German university medical centers (Charité Berlin, LMU/TUM Munich, Heidelberg/DKFZ, Tübingen, Freiburg, Frankfurt).
4. **Boundary Spanning**: High betweenness bridge researchers connect foundation-supported translational medicine with fundamental DFG-supported biological science.
